name: Sweet Corn
wateringNeeds: Deep watering, especially during silking and tasseling
description: A tall, warm-season grass crop grown for its sweet, edible kernels. It is wind-pollinated.
tips: For successful wind pollination, plant corn in a block of at least 4x4 rows, not in a single long row. Harvest when silks have turned brown and kernels are plump and milky.
succession: For a longer harvest, plant an early, a mid-season, and a late-season variety, or make succession plantings of the same variety every 2 weeks.

soil.type: Well-drained soil rich in organic matter.
soil.notes: Corn is a heavy feeder, especially of nitrogen. Amend soil well with compost or aged manure before planting.

temperature.notes: A warm-season crop that requires warm soil (at least 60°F) to germinate and grow. Very sensitive to frost.

environmentalAlerts.message: Cover with a blanket or bring potted plants indoors to protect from frost.

storage.notes: The sugars in sweet corn begin converting to starch immediately after picking. For best flavor, eat, freeze, or can it as soon as possible. Store in the husk in the refrigerator.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Once seedlings are 4-5 inches tall, thin them to stand about 12 inches apart in each direction.

careTasks.name: Side-dress with nitrogen
careTasks.description: When plants are about knee-high, apply a nitrogen-rich fertilizer alongside the rows to fuel their rapid growth.

careTasks.name: Monitor for corn earworm
careTasks.description: Check the silks for signs of the corn earworm caterpillar. A drop of mineral oil on the silks just after they pollinate can help deter them.

careTasks.name: Check for ripeness
careTasks.description: Harvest about 20 days after silks first appear. Silks should be brown and dry. Puncture a kernel with a fingernail; if the juice is milky, it's ready.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Corn is particularly thirsty during tasseling and silk development. The goal is to water deeply. Check for dryness by inserting your finger 1-2 inches into the soil. Consistent moisture is key for well-filled ears.
